newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end shade lower in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end shade lower in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Blue chips stocks finished with small losses at Bombay bourses on Tuesday as speculators offloaded stocks in a day that lacked any major action, dealers said.
"There was not much institutional business..fresh selling by speculators dragged down the market..," said a dealer at an institutional brokerage firm.
"Speculators tried to push up prices in mid-session but turned sellers at the close," he added.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) 30-share index rose to an early high of 3,429.37, but ended weak at provisional 3,384.19, a net loss of 5.30 points over Monday's close.
Dealers said apart from some scattered buying by foreign funds, market activity was generally sluggish.

Merrill Lynch and Indian affiliate DSP Financial Consultants in a strategy report titled, "A Roller Coaster Ride?" on Monday said Bombay's benchmark index is likely to touch 3800-4000 points in 1997 as improving fundamentals encourage foreign fund inflows.

"We expect the combination of good performance from the agricultural sector and the lagged benefits of easier monetary policy to feed through into better overall economic performance in the second half of calendar 1997, supporting a solid recovery in earnings in 1997/98 (April-March)," Merrill said.
Pivotal stocks at the BSE ended a tad above closing rates at the National Stock Exchange, (NSE) a pointer to the speculative sell-off at the NSE on its last day of weekly trade, dealers said.
The 50-stock NSE index hit the day's high of 980.15, but finished lower at 961.45, shedding 15.55 points or 1.59 percent, to a provisional 961.45.
At the BSE, ACC fell 46.20 rupees to 1,325.0, Indian Hotels 12.0 to 705.25, ITC 1.75 to 395.0 and TISCO 1.50 to 186.25.
SBI however rose 2.75 rupees to 275.50, Reliance 0.25 to 236.0, Bajaj Auto 14.70 to 906.50 and MTNL 4.50 to 239.0.
